grammar.en: "New Year in Japan" by Maria Lopez. I spent this New Year at my host family's house. On the morning of January 1st, we all said "Happy New Year." Then we ate the osechi food the host mother made. It was beautiful and very tasty. After the meal, we went to a nearby shrine. There were a lot of people, and we waited in line for about 30 minutes. At night, I called my family back home on my phone. When I talked about New Year in Japan, my mother said, "Sounds fun. Send me photos." Next New Year I plan to go back to my country, but someday I would like to spend New Year in Japan again.

reading.en: "My Family and the Cherry Blossoms" by Li Wei. This is my second spring since coming to Japan. Last spring I went cherry-blossom viewing at a famous park with university friends. The blossoms were beautiful, but there were too many people and I couldn't look at them slowly. This year my parents came from my country to visit. They were looking forward to seeing the blossoms, but in the week before they came, rain and strong wind continued and many blossoms fell. I was very disappointed. But the manager at my part-time job told me about a small town near the mountains. It is colder there than the town where I live, so the cherry trees bloom a little later. It took two hours by train, but when we went, the blossoms were at their very best. There weren't many people, and I could talk slowly with my parents while eating bento near the river. My father took lots of photos and sent them right away to my grandmother back home. She sent a message: "Next year I want to go to Japan too."

listening.en: A woman and a man are talking. F: It's become really cool. I like autumn best, because the food is delicious. M: I like autumn too. The food is good, but what I look forward to most is seeing the trees on the mountains turn red and yellow. F: Then let's go to the mountains together sometime.
listening.why: Food is the woman's favorite; the man likes seeing the leaves change color most.

listening.setup: {友|とも}だちが{結婚|けっこん}しました。
listening.question: {何|なに}と{言|い}いますか。
options: ご{結婚|けっこん}、おめでとうございます。
ご{結婚|けっこん}、ありがとうございます。
ご{結婚|けっこん}、お{疲|つか}れさまでした。
listening.en: Your friend got married. What do you say? 1. Congratulations on your marriage. 2. Thank you for your marriage. 3. Good work on your marriage.
listening.why: おめでとうございます is how you congratulate someone.

listening.setup: {友|とも}だちの{充電器|じゅうでんき}を{使|つか}いたいです。
listening.question: {何|なに}と{言|い}いますか。
options: {充電器|じゅうでんき}、{貸|か}してあげようか。
{充電器|じゅうでんき}、{借|か}りてもいい？
{充電器|じゅうでんき}、{借|か}りてくれる？
listening.en: You want to use your friend's phone charger. What do you say? 1. Shall I lend you my charger? 2. Can I borrow your charger? 3. Will you borrow a charger for me?
listening.why: {借|か}りてもいい？ asks permission to borrow.

listening.setup: お{祭|まつ}りで、{知|し}らない{人|ひと}に{自分|じぶん}の{写真|しゃしん}をとってほしいです。
listening.question: {何|なに}と{言|い}いますか。
options: すみません、{写真|しゃしん}をとってもいいですか。
すみません、{写真|しゃしん}をとりましょうか。
すみません、{写真|しゃしん}をとっていただけませんか。
listening.en: At a festival, you want a stranger to take your photo. What do you say? 1. Excuse me, may I take a photo? 2. Excuse me, shall I take a photo for you? 3. Excuse me, could you take a photo for me?
listening.why: ～ていただけませんか politely asks someone to do something for you.

listening.setup: {電話|でんわ}で、{相手|あいて}の{声|こえ}がよく{聞|き}こえません。
listening.question: {何|なに}と{言|い}いますか。
options: すみません、もう{少|すこ}し{大|おお}きい{声|こえ}でお{願|ねが}いします。
すみません、もう{少|すこ}し{小|ちい}さい{声|こえ}で{話|はな}しましょうか。
すみません、よく{聞|き}いてください。
listening.en: On the phone, you can't hear the other person well. What do you say? 1. Sorry, could you speak a little louder? 2. Sorry, shall I speak a little more quietly? 3. Sorry, please listen carefully.
listening.why: You ask the other person to speak louder.

listening.setup: {一月|いちがつ}{一日|ついたち}に、ホストファミリーのお{父|とう}さんに{会|あ}いました。
listening.question: {何|なに}と{言|い}いますか。
options: あけましておめでとうございます。
listening.en: On January 1st, you meet your host father. What do you say? 1. Have a good New Year (said before the New Year). 2. Happy New Year. 3. Take care of yourself (to someone sick).
listening.why: あけましておめでとうございます is the greeting after the New Year starts.

lines.jp: {結婚式|けっこんしき}の{写真|しゃしん}、{見|み}せてもらえますか。

listening.question: {何|なん}と{答|こた}えますか。
options: ええ、{見|み}せてもらいました。
いいえ、{見|み}ませんでした。
listening.en: F: Could I see the wedding photos? 1. Sure, go ahead. 2. Yes, they showed them to me. 3. No, I didn't see them.
listening.why: She is asking to see the photos, so 'Sure, go ahead' fits.

lines.jp: スマホの{電池|でんち}、もうすぐなくなりそう。

listening.question: {何|なん}と{答|こた}えますか。
options: じゃ、{充電器|じゅうでんき}、{貸|か}そうか。
うん、ちょっと{多|おお}すぎるね。
listening.en: M: My phone battery is about to die. 1. That's good. 2. Then shall I lend you a charger? 3. Yeah, it's a bit too much.
listening.why: Offering a charger is the natural reply to a dying battery.

lines.jp: {夏休|なつやす}みは、どこかへ{行|い}きましたか。

listening.question: {何|なん}と{答|こた}えますか。
options: はい、どこへも{行|い}きませんでした。
いいえ、{海|うみ}へ{行|い}きました。
はい、{家族|かぞく}と{海|うみ}へ{行|い}きました。
listening.en: F: Did you go anywhere in the summer holidays? 1. Yes, I didn't go anywhere. 2. No, I went to the sea. 3. Yes, I went to the sea with my family.
listening.why: Only 'Yes, I went to the sea with my family' matches はい/いいえ with the content.

lines.jp: お{母|かあ}さんの{具合|ぐあい}はどうですか。

listening.question: {何|なん}と{答|こた}えますか。
options: おかげさまで、だいぶよくなりました。
お{大事|だいじ}にしてください。
listening.en: M: How is your mother feeling? 1. Thank you, she's much better. 2. Please take care. 3. Yes, nice to meet you.
listening.why: He asks about her mother's health, so she answers how her mother is.

lines.jp: このアプリ、どうやってダウンロードするか、わかる？

listening.question: {何|なん}と{答|こた}えますか。
options: うん、ダウンロードしたことがないよ。
ううん、もう{知|し}ってるよ。
うん、ここを{押|お}せばいいよ。
listening.en: F: Do you know how to download this app? 1. Yeah, I've never downloaded it. 2. No, I already know. 3. Yeah, you just press here.
listening.why: Only option 3 says yes and then explains how.

lines.jp: お{正月|しょうがつ}は、{国|くに}へ{帰|かえ}るんですか。

listening.question: {何|なん}と{答|こた}えますか。
options: いいえ、{帰|かえ}ってきました。
ええ、{久|ひさ}しぶりに{家族|かぞく}に{会|あ}います。
ええ、{日本|にほん}に{来|き}てよかったです。
listening.en: M: Are you going back to your country for New Year? 1. No, I came back. 2. Yes, I'll see my family for the first time in a while. 3. Yes, I'm glad I came to Japan.
listening.why: Going home to see family answers the question.

lines.jp: すみません、ここで{写真|しゃしん}をとってもいいですか。

listening.question: {何|なん}と{答|こた}えますか。
options: はい、とってもらいました。
いいえ、とりませんでした。
すみません、ここはちょっと…。
listening.en: F: Excuse me, may I take photos here? 1. Yes, someone took one for me. 2. No, I didn't take any. 3. Sorry, here is a bit... (not allowed).
listening.why: Option 3 is a polite way to say photos are not allowed.

lines.jp: {来週|らいしゅう}の{誕生日|たんじょうび}パーティー、{来|こ}られる？

listening.question: {何|なん}と{答|こた}えますか。
options: うん、{来|き}てくれてありがとう。
ごめん、その{日|ひ}はちょっと{用事|ようじ}があるんだ。
うん、{来|こ}られてよかったね。
listening.en: M: Can you come to the birthday party next week? 1. Yeah, thanks for coming. 2. Sorry, I have something to do that day. 3. Yeah, good that you could come.
listening.why: He asks if she can come; only option 2 answers that.
